 * AMQP 0-9-1

 * STOMP 1.0 through 1.2

escaping each part separately, and then joining them. Any other form of
username is escaped as before.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: STOMP: settle deliveries independently of the subscription table
historicalFixesSummary.body:
ACK and NACK resolved delivery tags through the subscription table, so a
delivery settled after its subscription was gone was rejected and
stranded unsettled until the connection closed, burning a quorum-queue
delivery-limit attempt on the requeue at disconnect. The table is also
the wrong source: a subscription id may be reused with a different ack
mode, and the governing mode is the one in force at delivery.

The pending-ack ledger already holds what settlement needs, so record
the ack mode there too and settle from the ledger alone, matching the
subscription and tag from the ack id; a cumulative ack still prunes
older deliveries across subscriptions. An unmatched tag reports "Message
not found" rather than crashing frame processing through a miscalled
error/3, and a settlement queued in a transaction is skipped at commit
if already settled.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: STOMP: authorize durable subscription cleanup, take its queue from state
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The queue a durable UNSUBSCRIBE deletes was taken from the frame:
rabbit_stomp_util:subscription_queue_name/3 returns a client-supplied
x-queue-name header verbatim, and the plugin-local delete helper
performed no permission check, with if_unused and if_empty both false.
Any client permitted to subscribe could therefore delete any queue in
its own vhost while holding no permission on it, on a subscription that
need not itself be durable.

This affects main only: on 4.3.x and earlier the same cleanup issues
queue.delete on the client's own AMQP channel, where rabbit_channel
enforces configure permission.

Take the queue from #subscription.queue_name, recorded at SUBSCRIBE,
where the declare is already checked against configure permission.
Delete it as rabbit_channel does queue.delete: check configure
permission, then rabbit_amqqueue:delete_with/6, which also applies
check_internal/2 and check_exclusive_access/2. The permission check is
uncached because this module never invalidates its permission cache.

delete_with/6 raises where the plugin-local helper returned ok:
{absent, Q, timeout}, with/4's retry budget exhausted, and
{absent, Q, alive}, the queue process unexpectedly alive after the
delete exited, now end the connection with a not_found ERROR rather
than being swallowed as success. A crashed or stopped queue is still
force-deleted.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream coordinator: back off writer-shutdown replica failures and wake parked members for re-election
historicalFixesSummary.body:
When a replica start races the writer shutting down (its node restarting),
osiris:start_replica fails with {{shutdown, writer_unavailable}, _} or
{{shutdown, noproc}, _}. backoff_class/1 did not match these shapes, so they
fell through to 'none' and the coordinator re-drove the start immediately - a
hot loop (hundreds of failed start attempts per second per stream) that floods
the logs and delays streams reaching quorum+1 online. This was visible as a
multi-minute stall in a rolling cluster restart, where the per-node
await_online_quorum_plus_one gate waited on a few churning streams.

Classify {{shutdown, _}, _} as 'short' so the member parks instead of
hot-looping. The writer-down that follows drives the re-election.

For the parked member to take part in that re-election, set_running_to_stopped/1
now also wakes a timed park ({sleeping, RetryAt} -> current = undefined) so the
member is stopped in the current stop phase rather than waiting for its retry
timer; the stale parked-tree entry is dropped on the next reconcile. A
{sleeping, nodeup} park is left alone (its node is down, so it cannot be
stopped until the node returns). The writer-down handler now routes through
set_running_to_stopped/1 instead of an inline copy, so it gets the same wake.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream coordinator: make node reconnection O(footprint) not O(total cardinality)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The apply({nodeup, Node}) path was the last major deterministic command whose
cost scaled with total streams and total SAC groups rather than with the work
the event actually implies. On every partition heal, rolling restart or node
bounce it ran on all replicas and folded the entire streams and groups maps,
blocking the coordinator state machine.

Stream side (v8-gated): replace the blanket three-pass scan (re-monitor fold +
update_stream fold + evaluate_stream on every stream) with a single guarded
fold that touches only streams whose member on Node was parked for the nodeup
(a disconnected replica to resume and re-monitor, or a member sleeping on
'nodeup'). Streams with nothing parked on Node cannot change and are skipped.
The pre-v8 clause is kept for mixed-version clusters and log replay.

SAC side (v8-gated): add handle_node_reconnected/4. As of v8 a node
disconnection keeps the connection in pids_groups, so the reverse index is
already correct; the new path skips the compute_node_pid_group_dependencies
group scan and the merge, folding pids_groups keys filtered by node
(O(connections on the node)) to re-issue the monitor and check-connection
effects, leaving state untouched. Below v8 it delegates to /3.

Also in this change:
 - determinism: the consumer timestamp read by state_enter/2 (to size the
   disconnected timer) is now sourced from the command metadata system_time at
   v8+ via csr_status/3 and disconnect_ts/1, instead of reading the node wall
   clock inside apply, which diverged across replicas and on log replay
 - replace an O(n^2) survivor-list rebuild in handle_group_after_connection_down
   (tail append inside a fold) with lists:partition/2
 - fix two pre-existing SAC mock tests that expected apply/2 and
   ensure_monitors/4 while the v5+ dispatch calls apply/3 and ensure_monitors/5

  SAC handle_node_reconnected:

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream coordinator: fix writer liveness edge cases
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Address several liveness gaps in the deterministic apply/3 logic. All
behavioural changes are gated on machine version 8 so mixed-version
clusters stay deterministic; the pre-v8 paths are unchanged.

Level-triggered writer recovery: leader election was only ever driven by a
member_stopped event completing a quorum. A stream that should be running
could settle with no usable writer but a stopped quorum available (for
example after members are removed one by one while a majority of nodes are
unavailable), with no event left to trigger election and no way to recover
even via restart_stream/add_replica. The election is now factored into
stopped_in_epoch/1 + promote_writer/3, and recover_leaderless_stream/2 runs
before every stream evaluation to elect a writer from a stopped quorum when
the stream has no active writer, no member mid-action, and a candidate
stopped in the current epoch. The check is conservative so it never
preempts the normal recovery flow nor elects below quorum.

restart_stream no longer resurrects a member that is being deleted: it
previously reset every member's target to stopped, which could leave two
members with a writer role and crash find_leader/1 (and thus apply/3) with
a case_clause.

Stale start latches ({starting, _}) from an in-flight start that a
re-election raced are now cleared, both when the late member_started is
received and during the epoch transition, so the member is stopped and
restarted in the current epoch instead of remaining stuck until the next
coordinator leader change.

A replica marked disconnected after a noconnection DOWN is resumed as
running on nodeup, rather than staying disconnected until the next
stop/restart cycle.

The unreachable leader-delete branch in evaluate_stream emitted a
delete_member action with a bare node instead of an args map; corrected
defensively.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream coordinator: fix liveness gaps in the state machine
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Fix three issues in the deterministic apply/3 logic. The two behavioural
changes are gated on machine version 8 to keep mixed-version clusters
deterministic.

1. A replica whose 'start' action was in flight when a re-election advanced
   the stream epoch would receive a member_started carrying the old epoch.
   With no matching clause this was silently swallowed, leaving the member
   stuck with current = {starting, _} until the next coordinator leader
   change ran fail_active_actions/2. A stale member_started now clears the
   'starting' marker so the member is stopped and restarted in the current
   epoch.

2. A replica marked 'disconnected' after a noconnection DOWN was never
   resumed on nodeup: it stayed disconnected until the next stop/restart
   cycle. It is now resumed to running on nodeup, relying on the re-issued
   process monitor to restart it if the process did not survive the outage.

3. The (unreachable) leader-delete branch in evaluate_stream emitted a
   delete_member action with a bare node instead of an args map, which
   handle_aux would drop. Correct the action shape defensively.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: OAuth 2: rework parts of X-Forwarded-* header support #17153
historicalFixesSummary.body:
A few #17153 tweaks without major changes

\## Query String Support

No widely used proxy relies on query strings, so
we don't have to support it.

\## X-Forwarded-* Value Order

The original implementation in #17153 used the
leftmost value. With some proxies, this does not
matter but e.g. the very `httpd` used in our Selenium
tests support appended values, and the new (client-provided)
values end up on the left.

If we pick the rightmost option, chances are
we will pick the `httpd` configured setting and
not a client value.

Accidentally this addresses a comma-separated
value parsing bug that only specific inputs
triggered.

\## Improve Header Value Validation

Several scenarios, e.g. empty strings, resulted in
exceptions and 500 responses.

\## Refactoring, More Tests

Some functions have grown to take 6 arguments and yet
did not have a lot of test coverage.

\## ProxyRequests in the `httpd` Config

`ProxyRequests On` is a no-op without a <Proxy> section

so we can set it to the default value for
simplicity.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Shovel: report the specific reason a topology setup failure stops the worker
historicalFixesSummary.body:
`init_dest/1` and `init_source/1` can exit with a `{shutdown, _}`
reason to signal an expected condition, e.g. a predeclared queue is
missing or (for 'delete-after' Shovels) that there is nothing left to
transfer.

The catch-all clause in `handle_cast(init_shovel, ...)` caught every
exception raised during topology setup, including these `{shutdown, _}`
exits, and replaced them with a generic "failed to set up topology"
status. This discarded the specific reason before `terminate/2` had a
chance to report it.

Generalize the existing special case for `{shutdown, autodelete}` to
any `{shutdown, _}` reason, so `terminate/2` reports the actual reason.
Reasons that are not already wrapped in `{shutdown, _}` still fall
through to the generic clause, so unexpected errors are not logged
with a full stack trace.

This makes the following tanzu-rabbitmq suite green:
```
make -C deps/rabbitmq_shovel ct-stream_dynamic FULL=1
```

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream: add max_uncompressed_sub_entry_batch_size setting
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The broker stores a published sub-entry batch as-is, including its
declared uncompressed size, without decompressing or verifying it: doing
so would defeat the point of end-to-end sub-entry compression.

Add a per-node setting, max_uncompressed_sub_entry_batch_size, that
bounds this declared size at publish time. It defaults to 67108864
(64 MiB), matching the default of the same setting on the Java client
(maxUncompressedSubEntryBatchSize). Configure it via
stream.max_uncompressed_sub_entry_batch_size in rabbitmq.conf; the
broker and the clients publishing to it should use the same value,
since the broker's setting governs what can be written and a client's
setting governs what it will read back.

A publish frame with a sub-entry batch over the limit gets a
publish_error with the existing precondition_failed response code
instead of being stored. If one sub-entry in a frame is rejected, the
rest of that frame is rejected too, so a publisher never sees a gap in
its publishing ID sequence.

Also fixes a bug found while making this change: a publish_v2 frame with
no filter value, addressed to an unknown publisher ID, crashed the reader
instead of returning a publish_error.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream: enforce frame_max on outbound Deliver frames
historicalFixesSummary.body:
frame_max is negotiated once at Tune and is meant to bound frame size
in both directions, but only the inbound path enforced it. A Deliver
frame carries one whole osiris chunk as a single frame, with no
fragmentation, and chunk size is decided by osiris_writer's batching,
not by frame_max. A subscriber that negotiated a small frame_max could
therefore receive a Deliver frame bigger than what it agreed to.

The chunk is fixed size once committed by osiris and cannot be
re-encoded smaller for one connection, so the only option is to detect
and refuse: rabbit_stream_reader now compares each chunk's frame size
against the subscribing connection's frame_max before anything is
written to its socket, and closes the connection if it doesn't fit,
reusing the existing close/FRAME_TOO_LARGE wire pattern already used
for oversized inbound frames.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Static shovels: fix #17063
Federation: redact credentials from malformed-URI parse errors
historicalFixesSummary.body:
`amqp_uri:parse/2` returns `{error, {{unable_to_parse_uri, {malformed_uri,
RawURI, _}}, _}}` for a structurally malformed URI, embedding the raw URI
(including any `user:password@` userinfo) in the error `Info`. That `Info`
was logged verbatim via `~tp` in `log_skipped_link/3`, leaking credentials.

`sanitize_parse_error/1` now collapses this shape to a bare
`unable_to_parse_uri` atom, dropping both the raw URI and the exit stack
trace. The sanitized URI continues to be reported separately.

Extend the malformed-URI test to assert the error `Info`, not just the
`safe_uri`, is credential-free.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix `amqp_uri:remove_credentials/1` crash on malformed URIs
historicalFixesSummary.body:
`remove_credentials/1` calls `uri_parser:parse/2`, whose `-spec` documents
an `{error, no_scheme | {malformed_uri, ...}}` return, but it passed the
result straight to `proplists:get_value/2`. On a structurally malformed URI
the parser returns an error tuple, so `proplists:get_value` raised a
`function_clause`.

This function exists to sanitize a URI before logging it, so it is routinely
called on invalid input on error paths (federation link init, shovel
connection-failure logging). Crashing there defeats its purpose. Handle the
error return by falling back to a best-effort strip of the `user:password@`
userinfo, so credentials still never reach the logs.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Federation: isolate upstream URI parse errors at link init
historicalFixesSummary.body:
When a federation upstream URI fails to parse, `to_params/2` badmatched
`{ok, Params}` and crashed link initialisation. The crash propagated
through the link supervisor into broker recovery, so one malformed
upstream took the whole broker down on every cold boot.

The trigger is c3b950b3 (atom-table exhaustion hardening), which now
rejects unknown atom parameters (`auth_mechanism`, `verify`, ...) via
`list_to_existing_atom/1`. That hardening is kept as is; the regression
is that upstream definitions accepted by the older parser can now
return `{error, _}` and turn a per-link problem into a broker-wide
boot failure.

Make `to_params/2` return `{ok, _} | {error, {Info, SafeURI}}` with
credentials stripped, and have `init_link/1` log and return `ignore`
so one bad upstream cannot fail broker startup. Add unit tests covering
the parse-error return and the credential-stripping guarantee.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Parse AMQP 1.0 arrays in linear time
historicalFixesSummary.body:
All elements of an AMQP array share a single constructor which is encoded
once, in front of the first element. To parse an element, the parser
therefore has to put that constructor back in front of the element's bytes.

So far it prepended the constructor to the entire remainder of the array:

    parse_array_primitive(ElementType, Data) ->
        {Val, B} = parse(<<ElementType, Data/binary>>),
        {Val, B-1}.

Since Data holds all elements that are still to be parsed, every element
copied the remainder of the array once, making parsing an array of n
elements O(n^2).

Determine the size of a single element up front and cut only that element
out of the array, so that the copy is bounded by the element instead of by
the array. The size follows directly from the subcategory of the element's
constructor, that is from the high nibble of its format code [§1.6.1]:
subcategories 0x4 to 0x9 are fixed width, while 0xA to 0xF are prefixed by
one or four octets of size.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix flaky local_to_local_delete_dest_queue test
historicalFixesSummary.body:
This test deletes the shovel's destination queue and expects to
observe {terminated, dest_queue_down}. With the default
(non-predeclared) destination, the shovel detects the deleted queue,
reports that status, and then auto-recreates the queue on its very
next reconnect attempt, going back to `running'.

That next reconnect attempt used to be slowed down just enough by an
incidental crash dump (logged by gen_server2 for the previously
non-shutdown exit reason) for the test's polling to reliably catch the
transient {terminated, dest_queue_down} status in between. Now that
shovel workers exit with a quiet {shutdown, restart} reason instead
(see the exit-reason normalization in rabbit_shovel_worker), that
crash dump - and the delay it caused - is gone, and the shovel recovers
before the test ever observes the terminated status, making the test
flaky/failing.

Predeclare the destination queue and mark it as such in the shovel
config, so the shovel never tries to recreate it and every reconnect
attempt keeps failing instead of racing the shovel's own recovery.
This changes the stable, observable terminated reason from
dest_queue_down (the live monitor firing) to "failed to connect to
destination" (the generic reconnect failure), which the test now
asserts on.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix shovel status detail lost when normalizing exit reasons
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Normalizing every "please reconnect" exit path to the uniform
{shutdown, restart} reason (so the OTP layer stays quiet) meant the
specific detail describing why the shovel is restarting (e.g.
dest_queue_down, "heartbeat timeout", "failed to connect to
destination") was no longer available to terminate/2, which used to
report it via rabbit_shovel_status.

Report the specific reason via the new report_terminated/2 helper at
the point of detection, before it's discarded in favour of the
uniform {shutdown, restart} reason used to stop the process. The
terminate/2 clause for that reason no longer reports a generic status
itself, since doing so would overwrite the specific one just reported.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Revert shovel worker restart type back to permanent
historicalFixesSummary.body:
transient was introduced so the supervisor would only emit a
SUPERVISOR REPORT for genuinely abnormal terminations, relying on
shovel workers exiting with the literal {shutdown, restart} reason
for expected disconnects/reconnects.

That reason can be silently overridden: rabbit_shovel_worker only
starts trapping exits once both connections are established, so
while it is inside close_connections/1 during termination, an
'EXIT' signal from a not-yet-trapped, still-linked connection process
can arrive and replace the worker's own exit reason before the
supervisor ever sees {shutdown, restart}. Under permanent this is
harmless (it always restarts regardless of reason), but under
transient it can permanently stop a shovel from reconnecting.

Reverting to permanent for now; the underlying race needs a proper
fix (e.g. unlinking connections before the blocking close calls)
before transient can be reintroduced safely.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Reader: don't log a stack trace replying to an already-disconnected AMQP 1.0 peer
historicalFixesSummary.body:
handle_connection_frame replies to a peer-initiated close by sending our
own close frame. If the peer's socket is already gone by then (e.g. it
disconnected right after sending its own close, before our reply could
go out), that write throws {inet_error, closed}, which the generic
catch-all in handle_frame/4 turned into a full "Reader error" stack
trace logged at error level.

There is nobody left to notify and nothing more useful to do in that
case, so it doesn't warrant a stack trace - just a one-line note at
info level. Every other exception is unaffected and still gets the full
treatment.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Reader: log administrator-forced AMQP 1.0 connection closure as a warning
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The AMQP 1.0 equivalent of the AMQP 0-9-1 connection_forced fix: this
error description is only ever built by terminate/2 when a connection
is deliberately closed by an operator or by the broker itself
(rabbitmqctl close_connection, the management UI, maintenance mode
draining, a node-wide shutdown) - never in reaction to a client
protocol violation, so it does not warrant `error`-level logging. Every
other exception reaching handle_exception/3 is unaffected and still
logs at `error`.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: amqp10_client: don't report supervisor crashes for expected socket-close failures
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Every graceful-close path (an explicit {close, Reason}, receiving the
peer's close frame, and the connection reacting to a dependent process
exiting) already treated {error, closed} from send_close/send_open as
an expected, quiet outcome. Any other socket-level failure from the
same call (e.g. {error, einval}) fell through to {stop, Error, State},
using the raw, unwrapped error as the exit reason - which the
supervisor (transient, one_for_all) reports as an abnormal termination.

None of these represent a bug in the connection process: they're all
"we made a best-effort attempt to notify the peer we're closing, and it
failed for some socket-level reason" - there is nobody left to notify
and nothing more useful to do either way, regardless of which specific
reason the socket layer returned. All of these now fold into the same
quiet path as the existing {error, closed} handling.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: amqp10_client: fix deadlock in connection's own termination
historicalFixesSummary.body:
terminate/3 called sys:terminate(Sup, normal) - a blocking call from a
child process to its own direct supervisor - whenever the connection
stopped normally. When Sup tries to shut this same child down as part
of processing that call, it waits for the child to actually die; the
child is meanwhile blocked waiting for Sup to reply. Guaranteed
deadlock, timing out after 5 seconds on both sides: the supervisor logs
a shutdown_error/killed report once it gives up waiting, and the
connection process crashes with "State machine terminating" once its
own sys:terminate call times out.

This code path pre-dates the connection now properly reacting to a
dependent process dying (rather than lingering silently), which made it
far more likely to be hit in practice. The fix makes the sys:terminate
call fire-and-forget instead of blocking, preserving the intended
cleanup (tearing down the rest of the supervision tree) without the
connection waiting on it.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Reader: log administrator-forced connection closure as a warning
historicalFixesSummary.body:
connection_forced is only ever raised by rabbit_reader itself when a
connection is deliberately closed (rabbitmqctl close_connection, the
management UI, maintenance mode draining) - never by a client protocol
violation. It was going through the same generic hard-error path as
genuine exceptions, logging "Error on AMQP connection ..." at `error`
level for what is really just an intentional administrative action.

Every other exception reaching log_hard_error/3 (protocol violations,
permission errors, actual bugs) is unaffected and still logs at
`error`.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: amqp10_client: close connection gracefully when a dependent process exits
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The `opened` state had no clause for a linked process exiting (e.g.
the application code that opened the connection), so the event fell
through to the generic "unexpected connection frame" clause: a
confusing warning was logged and the connection was left open
indefinitely instead of being closed.

Added a clause that sends a proper AMQP close frame and transitions to
`close_sent`, mirroring the handling already used for the `{close,
Reason}` event.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: amqp_client: avoid crash dump when a dependent process exits
historicalFixesSummary.body:
amqp_network_connection treats any linked process exiting (e.g. the
application code that opened the connection) as a reason to close the
connection too, but built its own stop reason as a plain formatted
string rather than wrapping it in `{shutdown, _}`. Since this process
uses a plain gen_server, that meant terminate/2 printed a full
"** Generic server ... terminating" crash dump for what is normally
just the connection's owner shutting down.

amqp_direct_connection already handles the equivalent case correctly
(log and stop with `normal`); amqp_network_connection now does the
same, logging a concise warning and stopping with a `{shutdown, _}`
reason instead.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Shovel: share human-readable connection-failure logging across protocols
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The AMQP 0-9-1 shovel already translated raw connect errors (e.g.
econnrefused, nxdomain) into a human-readable one-line message. The
AMQP 1.0 shovel had no equivalent: a failed initial connection just
crashed on a badmatch, producing an opaque `{badmatch,{error,Reason}}`
in the log.

Moved the translation helper to rabbit_shovel_util so both protocol
modules share it, and made the AMQP 1.0 shovel check the result of
amqp10_client:open_connection/1 instead of pattern-matching on {ok, _}.

Logged at `warning` rather than `error`: a failed connection attempt
that will be retried on the next reconnect cycle isn't a critical
failure by itself.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Shovel: avoid noisy supervisor reports on expected reconnects
historicalFixesSummary.body:
A shovel disconnecting (e.g. a maintenance-mode connection close, a
heartbeat timeout) is a routine, retried event, not a crash. Until now
the worker exited with the specific failure reason, unwrapped, which
made the supervisor treat every such disconnect as an abnormal
termination and print a full SUPERVISOR REPORT. It also meant the
worker's own gen_server2 could print its own crash dump for the same
event, since only `{shutdown, _}` reasons are treated as expected.

All "please reconnect" exits now use the uniform `{shutdown, restart}`
reason, and the dynamic/static worker supervisors use `transient`
(instead of `permanent`) restart type, matching the pattern already
used by federation. `transient` still restarts unconditionally on the
explicit `{shutdown, restart}` sentinel, but only logs a report for
genuinely abnormal terminations. The specific failure is still logged
by the worker itself right before it stops, now at `warning` rather
than `error`, since it's an operational event the shovel recovers
from on its own rather than a critical failure.

Removed a handful of terminate/2 clauses that matched exit reasons no
longer produced anywhere in the module.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Encode AMQP 1.0 arrays of zero-octet elements as opaque values
historicalFixesSummary.body:
## What?

The AMQP 1.0 binary parser (amqp10_binary_parser) decoded an array
whose element constructor has a zero-octet wire encoding (null, true,
false, uint0, ulong0, list0 - wire codes 0x40-0x45) by expanding it
into a full Erlang list, one term per element, via lists:duplicate/2.
It now instead represents such an array as an opaque value ({as_is,
TypeCode, Bin}), the same representation already used for decimal and
NaN/Infinity values that RabbitMQ has no need to interpret further.

 ## Why

For this class of array, the element count is carried in a small,
fixed-size wire encoding, while the previous implementation allocated
one term per element when decoding it. This meant the memory needed to
hold the decoded value had no relationship to the size of the input
that produced it. Representing the value opaquely removes that
mismatch entirely, rather than merely capping it, and keeps the parser
consistent with how it already treats other value kinds it does not
need to interpret.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Add regression tests for UDS path Unicode encoding
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The UTF-8 handling for Unix domain socket paths in `ntoa/1`, `ntoab/1`
and `rabbit_json:encode/1` was verified only manually. A socket path
reaches these functions in two shapes: a Unicode charlist from a
config-defined listener and a UTF-8 binary from an accepted connection's
sockname. An earlier revision re-encoded the binary byte-by-byte, which
double-encoded non-ASCII paths, and `rabbit_json` had no clause for a
`{local, Path}` address at all, crashing on the empty-binary sockname of
an accepted UDS socket.

Add two cases to `unix_domain_socket_SUITE`. `test_uds_ntoa_non_ascii_path`
asserts a non-ASCII path normalises identically through `ntoa/1` and
`ntoab/1` for both input shapes. `test_uds_json_encode_local_address`
asserts `rabbit_json:encode/1` handles the empty-binary path and
non-ASCII paths in both shapes.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Format Unix domain socket paths as UTF-8 safely
historicalFixesSummary.body:
rabbit_misc:ntoa/1 and ntoab/1 render a {local, Path} address by calling
rabbit_data_coercion:to_list/1 and to_binary/1 respectively. Those helpers
mishandle Unix domain socket paths that are not plain ASCII:

  - A config-defined listener path arrives from cuttlefish as a Unicode
    charlist (codepoints). to_binary/1 (and list_to_binary/1 in the
    callers) raises badarg on any codepoint above 255, crashing the
    management listener listing and the certificate-expiration health
    check.
  - An accepted connection's peer path arrives as a UTF-8 binary (the
    accepted socket's sockname). to_list/1 turns it into a raw byte
    list, so it is no longer distinguishable from a codepoint charlist,
    and no single caller-side wrapper is correct for both shapes.

Fix the conversion at the source. ntoa/1 now uses to_unicode_charlist/1,
which yields a proper codepoint charlist for both the charlist and the
UTF-8 binary shape. ntoab/1 uses to_utf8_binary/1, which yields a correct
UTF-8 binary for both shapes and falls back to latin1 for paths that are
not valid UTF-8. Callers that need a binary (rabbit_mgmt_format:ip/1, the
certificate-expiration health check, and rabbit_core_metrics auth attempt
tracking) now build it with to_utf8_binary/1 over ntoa/1, and
rabbit_networking:tcp_host/1 routes the {local, _} case through ntoab/1
instead of duplicating the conversion.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix UDS address handling across auth, metrics, and listing surfaces
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The Unix domain socket support left the bare atom `local` leaking out of
two `rabbit_net:peername/1` destructure sites. An accepted UDS socket
reports `{ok, {local, <<>>}}`, but both sites matched `{ok, {Addr, _Port}}`,
collapsing the tuple into the atom `local`. That atom then reached
`is_loopback/1` and the auth data path, so scattered `local` atom clauses
had been added downstream to compensate.

Fix the two destructure sites to preserve the `{local, _}` tuple:
`rabbit_net:is_loopback/1` (socket clause) and
`rabbit_access_control:get_authz_data_from({socket, _})`. With the tuple
preserved, remove the now-dead symptom clauses `is_loopback(local)`,
`ntoa(local)` and `ntoab(local)`.

Widen the `rabbit_net:peername/1` and `sockname/1` specs to include
`inet:returned_non_ip_address()`, mirroring OTP, since an accepted UDS
socket genuinely returns `{ok, {local, Path}}`. This lets Dialyzer accept
the new `{ok, {local, _}}` clause, and the `socket_ends/2` Dialyzer
suppression is no longer needed.

Render a `{local, Path}` address in the CLI `list_connections` output: add
a `format_info_item/2` clause for it, mirroring the existing IPv4 and IPv6
tuple clauses, so the socket path is shown instead of the raw
`{local, ...}` tuple. This matches the HTTP API, which already formats it
via `rabbit_misc:ntoa/1`.

Correct the `ntoab/1` spec to `string() | binary()`, add `{local, string()}`
to the `peeraddr` type, and make `rabbit_mgmt_format:ipb/1` use
`iolist_to_binary/1` so a `{local, _}` address cannot crash it.

A UDS listener is configured with `local:/path:0` or `unix:/path:0`, which
the cuttlefish `domain_socket` datatype parses into `{local, Path, 0}`.

Split the test suite into `with_listener` and `without_listener` groups and
give the listener a single owner: `init_per_group`/`end_per_group` start and
stop it once for the group, per-testcase application environment moves into
`init_per_testcase`/`end_per_testcase`, and the test bodies only open
connections and assert. No test body or teardown calls `stop_tcp_listener`
on a listener whose existence it cannot guarantee, which removes the
`{error, not_found}` teardown crash seen under the parallel CT runner.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix stream SAC coordinator ignoring deactivating consumer status
historicalFixesSummary.body:
When a consumer's stepping-down consumer_update response triggers the
coordinator's command_activate_consumer handler, the deactivating
consumer is treated as active because is_active({_, DEACTIVATING}) is
true. The handler then sets all connected consumers to
{CONNECTED, WAITING} and calls evaluate_active_consumer/1, which picks
a new active. If that picks the same deactivating consumer, the
branch suppresses the needed notification effect, the coordinator
thinks the consumer is active while its client has already been told
active=false, and the result is a stuck partition that never delivers
messages. Checking for a deactivating consumer so we hit the
notification effect in that case fixes the bug.

Fixes #16975

Log mirrored_supervisor roster wipe and successful failover at info
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Two low-frequency, high-consequence mirrored_supervisor events were only
observable at debug (the roster wipe) or not at all (a successful failover),
while their failure counterparts are already logged. Both matter for federation
and shovel, whose link rosters live in mirrored_sup_childspec.

- init/delete_all: the branch that deletes all child records for a group (when
  this node is the sole reachable member) is the most destructive operation in
  the module. Promote its log from debug to info and reword it, so a wrong wipe
  (e.g. a node that transiently sees no peers) leaves a trace above debug.

- DOWN/failover: when a peer dies and this node re-homes and starts its children,
  the success path was silent; only the "could not start some children" and
  "failover failed" branches logged. Add an info log on success (guarded so a
  dead peer that owned no children does not log a no-op), symmetric with the
  existing failure logging.

Both are per-event (not per-child / per-start_child), so they do not add
steady-state noise. No behavior change.

Maintenance mode: drain and revive tolerate failing housekeeping callbacks
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Once rabbit_maintenance:drain/0 has marked the node as being drained, any
subsequent step is housekeeping around cleaning up in-flight state. A
plugin drain/1 callback that crashes, a channel that refuses to shut
down within the termination timeout, or a stuck federation link would
raise from inside drain/0 and surface at the CLI layer as a non-zero
exit code, even though the node was in fact drained. Automation like
Kubernetes preStop hooks that runs `rabbitmq-upgrade drain` treats that
as a failed drain and retries or aborts the upgrade.

Wrap each housekeeping step in a local safe_maintenance_step/2,3
helper that logs a warning with the stacktrace and continues. The
load-bearing mark_as_being_drained/0 call is intentionally left
unwrapped: if it fails, drain has not actually happened and the caller
must know.

Applied the same treatment to revive/0 so that a failing queue-type
revive callback or federation reconnect no longer leaves the DRAINING
flag stuck, which would keep the node effectively unusable.

Added a maintenance_mode_SUITE regression test that mecks
rabbit_queue_type:drain/1 and revive/0 to raise, then asserts that
drain/0 and revive/0 still return ok and the node's DRAINING flag
transitions as expected.

Closes #3369.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Management agent: tolerate non-integer values in metrics aggregation
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The mgmt metrics collector reads rows from the core_metrics ETS
tables on every scrape and feeds them through sum_entry/2 and
difference/2, which add or subtract tuples element-wise. Each
field is expected to be an integer.

Under connection or queue churn, a field can briefly read as the
empty atom '' — the same sentinel rabbit_mgmt_format uses to
represent "null". Performing arithmetic on it raises badarith
inside the gen_server, killing the collector for that table and
losing any in-progress aggregation state (#12815):

    exception error: an error occurred when evaluating an
                     arithmetic expression
        in operator  -/2
           called as '' - 19495760921
        in call from rabbit_mgmt_metrics_collector:difference/2

Wrap sum_entry/2 and difference/2 so each input tuple goes through
a normalisation pass first: if every element is an integer the
tuple is reused as-is; otherwise non-integer fields are coerced
to 0 and the rebuilt tuple is fed to the original arithmetic.
A single bad scrape now produces an imperfect delta instead of a
crash, and the next scrape recovers a correct value.

A regression test in metrics_SUITE.erl injects a synthetic Pid
into connection_coarse_metrics with one field set to '', runs
two scrapes via force_collect, and verifies the collector
process is still alive afterwards. A second unit-style test pins
down the "non-integer coerces to 0" contract.

Closes #12815.

Tolerate undefined/none decorators in `rabbit_queue_decorator:select/1`
historicalFixesSummary.body:
A queue whose stored `decorators` field is the atom `undefined` crashes
the broker at boot with `error:{bad_generator,undefined}` when a queue
decorator is registered (for example by the queue federation plugin),
because `select/1` is a list comprehension that assumes a list.

Quorum queues migrated from Mnesia to Khepri retain `decorators =
undefined`: the durable Mnesia record stored `undefined`, the migration
copies it verbatim, and quorum queues are not re-stored during recovery
the way classic queues are.

Add `undefined` and `none` clauses to `select/1` returning `[]`, matching
the existing guard in `rabbit_exchange_decorator:select/2`, and add a
unit test.

Fixes #16843

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Stream: log a clean message when a client RPC times out
historicalFixesSummary.body:
Previously, when rabbit_stream_reader detected an outstanding RPC
request (such as a consumer_update) that exceeded request_timeout,
it stopped the gen_statem with {request_timeout, _} as the exit
reason. OTP treats that as an abnormal exit, so the connection's
full state was dumped to the error log along with a gen_statem
stack trace for what is an expected operational condition.

Stop with {shutdown, {request_timeout, TimedOut}} instead so OTP
treats the exit as benign, and emit a single INFO log line that
names the connection plus the per-request content
(subscription_id, stream, consumer_name, active) of every request
that timed out.

Closes #15744.

The migration ties an auto-delete exchange to having at least one
outbound binding (that is, where the exchange in question
is the source) via a `keep_while` condition.

An exchange without such bindings (e.g. an exchange-to-exchange
destination or an `alternate-exchange` target) cannot satisfy it,
so Khepri rejects the write with `keep_while_conditions_not_met`.

Such exchanges should be skipped, matching the behavior
on the `exchange.declare` path.

historicalFixesSummary.subject: Fix SigV4 SignatureDoesNotMatch on body-less requests (e.g. S3 GET)
historicalFixesSummary.body:
The SigV4 signer includes "content-length" in the signed-header set for
every request, with value "0" when the body is empty. The body-less
request clause then calls httpc:request/4 with an empty options list, and
httpc strips the "content-length" header from a request that has no body
before sending it. The headers actually transmitted therefore no longer
match the signed-header set the signature was computed over, so the
service rejects the request with SignatureDoesNotMatch (HTTP 403).

This affects any empty-body request, most visibly S3 GetObject:
fetching an object via an S3 ARN fails every time, while body-bearing
requests (e.g. Secrets Manager GetSecretValue) are unaffected because
httpc preserves content-length when a body is present.

Pass {headers_as_is, true} to httpc on the body-less clause so the signed
headers, including "content-length: 0", are sent verbatim and match the
signature. The body-bearing clause is unchanged.

Verified against S3 (GetObject) and Secrets Manager (GetSecretValue):
with the fix the S3 GET succeeds; without it, S3 fails with
SignatureDoesNotMatch while Secrets Manager succeeds on the same
credentials.
